guidance.inspection: Read each return or destruction duty with its governing trigger. Support the hypothesis only when termination, expiry, completion, abandonment, or rejection of the relationship activates disposition; a request-only duty does not establish disposition upon termination. Retain all operative alternatives, objects, timing, and qualifying lead-ins.

Reconstruct the identification rule for every form of protected information. Entailment requires identification by the disclosing party across the definition's full scope; an alternative based on circumstances, reasonable understanding, or what the recipient should know defeats the universal requirement. Preserve form-specific timing and written-confirmation conditions.

any_phrases: should know is treated as confidential

guidance.inspection: Collect genuine independent-development permissions or exclusions and their no-access, no-use, proof, timing, and actor conditions. A prior-possession clause, acquisition from another source, or unrelated third-party dealing is not independent development. Retain both independently operative permissions and definition exclusions.

Locate an operative permission for the receiving party to disclose or provide access to its employees. Verify whose employees are covered and retain need-to-know, purpose, confidentiality-undertaking, and responsibility conditions. A recipient-class definition or mention of the disclosing party's employees is not itself permission.

Read no-grant, ownership, reservation, and affirmative-license language together. A limited use purpose, access to information, or disclosure permission is not by itself a grant of rights and does not oppose the hypothesis. An express licence or other affirmative right must be evaluated with its object, scope, duration, and any controlling reservation.

Inspect nondisclosure of the existence, occurrence, content, timing, status, or terms of negotiations, discussions, an agreement, or the contemplated transaction. Retain the operative prohibition and its consent, audience, law, or regulatory exceptions. Exclude neighboring items concerning only received materials or unrelated confidential information.

Determine whether identified contractual obligations continue after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, return, or destruction. Retain the affected duties, duration, endpoint, and exceptions. A termination right, accrued-rights clause, general severability clause, or obligation ending on a stated date does not alone establish post-termination survival.

Read the legal, regulatory, subpoena, court-order, or similar compulsion together with the duty to notify the disclosing party. Verify actor, trigger, timing, legal-permission qualification, and opportunity for protection. Reject unauthorized-use notices and bare permissions to disclose compelled information.

all_phrases: as much notice of this disclosure as possible

guidance.inspection: Identify a restriction on the receiving party soliciting, recruiting, hiring, employing, or initiating employment contact with personnel connected to the disclosing party. Read forward through split target lists and exceptions, retaining actor, target class, duration, approval condition, and general-advertising or unsolicited-contact exceptions. Reject proxy solicitation and exception-only hits.

Determine whether the text affirmatively permits or necessarily contemplates creating copies in a stated circumstance. Distinguish that permission from retaining existing copies and from a bare prohibition on copying, even when consent could remove the prohibition. Retain the operative permission or restriction, its purpose, actor, object, and conditions.

Inspect whether information or copies may remain after an otherwise applicable return, destruction, or deletion process. Capture archival, backup, legal, regulatory, evidentiary, and impracticability exceptions with their continuing duties. Treat an express no-retention or exhaustive all-copies disposition as opposition; an ordinary return duty alone need not settle retention.

Read only definitional or inclusion language that establishes protected subject matter. Decide whether non-technical categories are affirmatively included; business, financial, marketing, personnel, contact, or general commercial information opposes a technical-only definition. Do not use exclusions, use restrictions, or an unconnected actor mention as definitional evidence.

Determine whether the protected-information definition includes information conveyed orally or verbally. Retain the governing definition and any identification or later-writing condition that limits oral coverage. Do not infer oral coverage merely from a broad subject list or an exclusion heading.

any_phrases: irrespective of the form of communication

guidance.inspection: Find an exclusion or affirmative right covering information obtained from a source other than the disclosing party. Verify third-party provenance, lawful or legitimate receipt, absence of confidentiality duties, and any knowledge or inquiry condition. Mere permission to negotiate with third parties or an independent-development clause does not establish acquisition of similar information.

Locate an operative permission or closed-class restriction governing disclosure to non-employee recipients such as agents, consultants, counsel, advisers, contractors, or other representatives. Retain need-to-know, purpose, undertaking, consent, and responsibility limits. Employee-only permission can oppose broader third-party sharing; a recipient definition alone is not permission.

Identify an operative restriction limiting use of protected information to the agreement's stated transaction, evaluation, project, or other purpose. Retain the governing actor, protected object, purpose, consent exceptions, and independently repeated restrictions. Do not treat disclosure limits, ownership clauses, or recipient responsibility as use limits.

Inspect any prohibition on reverse engineering or closely specified technical decomposition of an object embodying protected information. Verify the bound actor, prohibited act, covered object, confidentiality connection, and exceptions. Do not infer reverse engineering from independent development, legitimate acquisition, ordinary analysis, or return and destruction duties.

Verify that termination, expiry, completion, abandonment, or rejection triggers return or destruction. A request-only duty is insufficient. Retain the governing trigger, disposition alternatives, objects, timing, and qualifications.
